statement: Ana eats one third of a cake. Then Bo eats half of what is left. What fraction of the whole cake is left now?

choices.misconception: I took a third and a half of the whole cake away, but Bo ate half of what was left, not half of the cake.
I only thought about Bo eating half and forgot that Ana had already eaten some.
I worked out what was left after Ana and forgot that Bo ate some too.
I added a third and a half to find the cake that was eaten, then gave that instead of what is left.

hints: Draw the cake as a bar cut into three equal pieces.
A fraction of a remainder: work out what is left after Ana, then Bo eats half of that leftover, not half of the whole cake. A picture keeps track of the whole.
After Ana, two thirds are left. Half of two thirds is one third.

solutions.reliable: Cut the cake into 3 equal pieces. Ana eats 1 piece, leaving 2. Bo eats half of those 2 pieces, which is 1 piece, leaving 1 piece. One piece out of 3 is 1/3 of the cake. The transferable idea: when a fraction is "of what is left", redraw the leftover and take the fraction of that.
solutions.elegant: Bo eats half of what is left, so he leaves exactly as much as he eats. After Ana, 2/3 of the cake remains, and Bo and the leftover share it equally: 1/3 each.

whyOnTest: "Half of what is left" is not "half of the cake", so this tests whether a fraction is taken of the right whole.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
